instruction: Find the latest message in the Bills local folder and transfer it to the 'have_seen' subfolder under Local Folders.

args.query: title = 'attachment' and 'root' in parents and trashed = false

rules.expected_moved_message: Confirm your email to get started on X

metadata.explanation: Task requires moving the newest message (X/Twitter email from Jan 12, 2024, verified from cache data) from Bills to have_seen folder. Bills initially has 2 messages. After moving the newest message, Bills should have 1 message remaining (the AWS email from Jan 3) and have_seen should have 1 message (the moved X/Twitter email). Evaluator verifies: (1) folder counts match expected values, and (2) the message in have_seen is the correct one (X/Twitter confirmation email with subject 'Confirm your email to get started on X').

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies ALL instruction requirements: (1) folder count changes indicate a message was moved, and (2) the specific message in have_seen matches the expected most recent message subject

Getter logic is semantically correct: parses mbox files, extracts Date headers from emails using email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime, sorts messages by date to identify most recent, and captures subjects from have_seen folder (thunderbird.py:10-115)

Metric logic is semantically correct: verifies folder counts match expected values AND checks that the message in have_seen is the expected message 'Confirm your email to get started on X' (thunderbird.py:8-86, lines 60-75)

Expected values are correct: Bills should have 1 remaining (AWS email from Jan 3), have_seen should have 1 (X/Twitter email from Jan 12), and the moved message subject is correctly specified as the X/Twitter confirmation email

Data flow is correct: Getter extracts have_seen_subjects list → Metric verifies have_seen has exactly 1 message AND that message matches expected_moved_message → Returns 1.0 only if both conditions met
Edge cases handled: Metric checks for None result (line 21-23), empty have_seen folder (line 84-85), wrong count (line 80-82), and wrong message moved (line 74-75)
The evaluator can distinguish correct from incorrect executions: if wrong message moved, metric returns 0.0 (line 74-75); if correct message moved with correct counts, returns 1.0 (line 72)
